keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «실크로드로 옮겨진 가장 중요한 것은 물건이 아니었다(주장)» 와 «문화 사이의 교류가 언제나 인류의 역사를 만들어 왔다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the claim (the most important things carried on the Silk Road were not products) and the conclusion (exchange between cultures has always shaped human history). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: The Silk Road, a network that linked East and West

boxes.qen: How did goods travel on the Silk Road?
boxes.a: From merchant to merchant through oasis cities
Ideas, religions, and even diseases spread between cultures

sumHowto.ko: 먼저 위 세 칸을 보고, 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 고르세요.
sumHowto.en: Look at the three boxes, then choose the right word for each blank.

sum.pre: The Silk Road was not one road but a

, religions, and technologies. Buddhism spread to Korea, and sadly,

words: It was not one road but a network of land and sea routes used for well over a thousand years.
a group of connected roads, lines, or people
goods were passed from merchant to merchant through busy oasis cities
a person who buys and sells goods

qs.q: Why is the name "Silk Road" a little misleading?
qs.qko: «실크로드» 라는 이름은 왜 조금 오해를 부를 수 있나요?
opts: It was not one road but a network of land and sea routes
Silk was never sold along these routes
Marco Polo gave it the wrong name
evs: It was not one road but a network of land and sea routes used for well over a thousand years.
In the nineteenth century, a German geographer named it the Silk Road, after one of its most famous goods.
Few traders ever made the whole journey.
In a way, it was the world's first great network, and today's global connections continue its story.
why: 본문에 «It was not one road but a network of land and sea routes» 라고 나와요. 하나의 길이 아니라 여러 길이 이어진 연결망이었기 때문에 이름이 오해를 부를 수 있어요.
The text says it was not one road but a network of land and sea routes, so the name can give the wrong idea.

qs.q: What does the writer mean by saying the most important things carried on the Silk Road "were not products at all"?
qs.qko: 글쓴이가 실크로드로 옮겨진 가장 중요한 것은 «물건이 전혀 아니었다» 고 한 것은 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: Ideas, religions, and technologies mattered more than the goods
The merchants did not carry any goods at all
Only silk was valuable enough to trade
evs: Ideas, religions, and technologies traveled with the merchants.
Spices, paper, and porcelain also traveled along the routes.
Instead, goods were passed from merchant to merchant through busy oasis cities such as Samarkand.
Long before airplanes and the internet, a web of routes connected East Asia with the Mediterranean world.
why: 바로 다음 문장에서 생각, 종교, 기술이 상인들과 함께 이동했다고 해요. 물건보다 이런 것들이 더 중요했다는 뜻이에요.
The next sentence says ideas, religions, and technologies traveled with the merchants. These mattered more than products.

qs.q: How was ancient Korea connected to the Silk Road?
qs.qko: 옛 한국은 실크로드와 어떻게 이어져 있었나요?
opts: Buddhism reached Korea, and glass from distant lands was found in Silla tombs
Korean silk was the most famous good sold in Rome
Korean merchants made the whole journey to Venice
evs: Buddhism spread from India into China and later reached Korea and Japan.
Even ancient Korea was connected, as glass objects from distant lands have been found in Silla tombs.
Papermaking moved west from China, eventually helping books spread in Europe.
Chinese silk was highly valued in Rome, and in return goods such as glass, silver, and horses moved east.
why: 불교가 인도에서 중국을 거쳐 한국과 일본까지 왔고, 신라 무덤에서는 먼 나라의 유리 물건이 발견되었어요. 두 단서를 합치면 옛 한국도 실크로드로 이어져 있었다는 것을 알 수 있어요.
Buddhism spread from India into China and reached Korea, and glass objects from distant lands were found in Silla tombs. Together, these clues show the connection.

ends: How did Buddhism travel from India to Korea?
What treasures from faraway lands were found in Silla tombs?
신라 무덤에서 나온 먼 나라의 보물은 무엇일까?

write.howtoKo: 예문을 틀로 삼아, 빈칸 두 곳을 «해야 할 일 + 그 목적» 으로 바꿔 영어로 써 보세요.
write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write what we should do and the result you want in English.
write.src: “We should <u>learn about other cultures</u> so that <u>we can share ideas with people around the world</u>.”

write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «so that» 뒤에 «누가 + 무엇을 할 수 있는지» 를 넣어 결과를 분명하게 써 보세요. (예: so that we can make friends from other countries)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «so that», write who can do what. (e.g. so that we can make friends from other countries)
